metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) limited in practice Friday
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan returned to a limited practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: McMillan was back after he sat out of practice on Thursday. He is trending towards being good to go for Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Limited at Friday's practice
metadata.description: McMillan (foot) practiced in a limited capacity Friday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: McMillan's return to the practice field generally is a positive sign as he works through a sore foot, but he now has just one more chance to get back to full Saturday, at which point the Panthers may tag him with a designation for Monday's game at Tampa Bay. No matter, head coach Dave Canales has expressed optimism this week that McMillan will be able to go in Week 12, per Kaye.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Not in uniform Friday
metadata.description: Updating a previous report, McMillan (foot) took part in Friday's team stretch but wasn't in uniform, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Per Mike Kaye of ESPN.com, McMillan was in a helmet and pads as the Panthers made their way to the practice field Friday but ditched them by the time the team stretched. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - In uniform for Friday's practice
metadata.description: McMillan (foot) was wearing a helmet and pads ahead of Friday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: McMillan was listed as a DNP on Thursday's estimated injury report due to a sore foot, but his return one day later backs up head coach Dave Canales' expressed optimism to Kaye about the wide receiver's status for Week 12. Friday's practice report will reveal McMillan's activity level.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) misses practice Thursday
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan did not practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: McMillan did not participate in Thursday's walkthrough. He will need to be monitored in practice on Friday and Saturday.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Listed DNP on Thursday
metadata.description: McMillan (foot) was listed as a DNP on Thursday's practice estimate, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: After McMillan didn't participate in Wednesday's unofficial practice due to a sore foot, head coach Dave Canales told Kaye that the team is "optimistic" that the wide receiver will play Monday at Tampa Bay. McMillan will have two more chances to mix into drills this week before the Panthers potentially tag him with a designation for Week 12 action.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Canales 'optimistic' about Week 12 status
metadata.description: Head coach Dave Canales said Wednesday that the Panthers are "optimistic" that McMillan (foot) will play Monday in Tampa Bay, Mike Kaye of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: McMillan didn't partake in Wednesday's unofficial practice, after which Canales revealed that the wide receiver dealt with soreness in his foot after Sunday's win against the Ravens in which he hauled in six of nine targets for 71 yards and one touchdown. Considering the Panthers likely are practicing Wednesday in lieu of a session on Thanksgiving, McMillan appears likely to be listed as a DNP on the team's first Week 12 injury report Thursday.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Not present Wednesday
metadata.description: McMillan wasn't spotted at Wednesday's unofficial practice, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Because the Panthers don't play until Monday at Tampa Bay, they won't be posting an injury report until Thursday, at which point a reason for practice restrictions, if any, for McMillan will become known. According to Person, McMillan limped off the field during this past Sunday's win against the Ravens but returned to action, so he may be dealing with a health concern as Carolina begins Week 12 prep.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Finds end zone in win over Baltimore
metadata.description: McMillan caught six of nine targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: The second-year wideout posted his best yardage total since Week 6 while leading the Panthers in receiving yards, catches and targets. McMillan capped his solid performance with a seven-yard TD from Bryce Young in the second quarter. McMillan has slowed down since a torrid start to the season, but he still sports a 55-731-4 line on 87 targets through 10 games heading into a Week 12 clash with the Buccaneers.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Bounces Back to Lead Panthers Pass-Catchers in Week 11
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan had a big game in his team's Week 11 win over the Baltimore Ravens, recording six catches for 71 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. It was a nice bounce-back performance for the 23-year-old, who was held to just three catches for 35 yards on seven targets by the New Orleans Saints in Week 10. McMillan had also been held to under 60 receiving yards in four straight contests entering Week 11. Still, McMillan is the clear number one option in the Carolina passing game and has had a solid year overall, hauling in 55 catches for 731 yards and four touchdowns on 87 targets across 10 games. While he may not quite have high-end WR1 upside most weeks, McMillan profiles as a must-start wide receiver for fantasy managers heading into Carolina's crucial Week 12 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan finds the end zone in Week 11 win
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 targets for 71 yards and one touchdown in a 35-33 win over the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: McMillan found the end zone on a seven yard reception in the second quarter, marking his fourth touchdown of the season. McMilan and the Panthers will take on Tampa Bay in a divisional matchup in Week 12.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Should Remain Set in Lineups as a WR2
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan continues to display inconsistency in production, even as the Panthers' clear top receiving option. McMillan caught three passes for 35 yards on seven targets in the Panthers Week 10 win versus the New Orleans Saints. He has 30 targets over his previous four games, but has only had a 57% catch rate, amounting to 189 receiving yards. He has been particularly lackluster in the touchdown category, only scoring three on the season. Despite a lack of fantasy production over these last four weeks, he has clear opportunity; his 30 targets put him 10th in targets among wide receivers. The Panthers' Week 11 opponent, the Baltimore Ravens, are middle of the road in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers. However, they have only allowed six touchdowns to wide receivers all year. This matchup isn't projected to be a high-scoring one, so performance expectations should be tempered. Fantasy managers likely can't and shouldn't try to get away from McMillan this week, though. His usage is favorable and enough to keep him as a low-end WR2, RotoBaller's WR20 in Week 11.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Held to three catches in win over Saints
metadata.description: McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.
metadata.analysis: The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan hauls in three passes in Week 10
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan caught 3-of-7 targets for 35 yards in a 20-17 win over the Saints.
metadata.analysis: McMillan led the team in targets with seven, but was only able to convert that into three receptions, his lowest total since Week 2. The 23-year-old will look to bounce back against Baltimore in Week 11.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Held to 35 Yards Versus Saints
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan recorded three receptions (on seven targets) for 35 yards (11.7 yards per reception) and no touchdowns in a 20-17 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 10. While McMillan led the team in targets, he finished third in receptions and third in receiving yards behind running back Chuba Hubbard (five receptions for 80 yards) and tight end Tommy Tremble (four catches for 48 yards). Quarterback Bryce Young was held to 200 passing yards against the New Orleans defense, so McMillan's low production is not a surprise. Still, the three catches and 35 yards marked the lowest totals for McMillan since Week 3 (two catches for 17 yards versus the Cleveland Browns). McMillan will continue to operate as Carolina's WR1, and there should not be many concerns about his production or usage moving forward.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Can Be Confidently Relied Upon vs. Saints
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan had a decent performance in Week 9 versus a tough Broncos' secondary, drawing six targets and catching four of them for 56 yards, with his fantasy day being saved by a five-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. McMillan and teammate Jalen Coker only received 11 targets combined as the premier pieces of the Panthers' passing attack, which is atypical, as McMillan has only seen six or fewer targets in three games through eight played. His usual substantial role has elevated him to WR14 in fantasy points per game this year. He has an easier task this week against a vulnerable Saints' defense, which is middle of the league in both fantasy points and touchdowns allowed to opposing wide receivers. Given that QB Bryce Young leads the NFL in pass attempts per game at 38.5, and the Saints Defense has allowed 27 points per game, McMillan should be in line for plenty of opportunities in Week 10. Fantasy managers can confidently start McMillan as a high-end WR2 in their Week 10 contest.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan scores touchdown in Week 9
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan caught four of six targets for 56 yards and one touchdown in the Panthers' 26-21 loss to the Broncos in Week 9.
metadata.analysis: McMillan caught a four-yard touchdown with just over three minutes remaining to pull Carolina within five points. He finished second on the Panthers in receiving yards behind Darren Waller, who saw 10 targets compared to McMillan's six. The touchdown helped, but Waller commanded more opportunities against Denver. McMillan remains a starting option in fantasy leagues heading into Week 10.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Salvages day with late TD
metadata.description: McMillan caught four of six targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
metadata.analysis: The second-year wideout caught Bryce Young's third TD of the afternoon, a four-yard toss late in the fourth quarter that gave the Panthers some late hope. It was McMillan's first trip to the end zone since Week 4, and through eight games he's collected a 46-625-3 line on 71 targets. He'll look to build on this performance in a Week 10 road trip to New Orleans.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Continues Consistent Play on Sunday
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan continued to find success during Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos. The 23-year-old hauled in four of his six targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the loss. This was the first time that McMillan was able to find the end zone since the Week 4 matchup against the Detroit Lions. He has now finished with 50 receiving yards or more in four of his last five games. The hope is that his success will continue against the shaky New Orleans Saints pass defense in Week 10. McMillan has been the most consistent receiver for this team, so he figures to continue being significantly involved.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Remains a Must-Start Wide Receiver
metadata.description: Across seven games in 2026, Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan has recorded 42 catches for 569 yards and two touchdowns on 65 targets. The 23-year-old has had a strangely difficult time getting in the end zone, as he's been held without a touchdown in every game other than his massive two-score outing against the Detroit Lions in Week 4. McMillan's production has also slowed down lately, as he's failed to reach 60 receiving yards in back-to-back games. However, McMillan remains a high-volume pass-catcher, as he saw 11 targets in Carolina's Week 8 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Despite his recent struggles, McMillan remains a must-start wide receiver for fantasy managers going forward.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan catches six passes in Week 8 loss
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan brought down 6-of-11 targets for 58 yards in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.
metadata.analysis: Fantasy managers in PPR formats were certainly okay with McMillan's performance in this one. The volume was there, but the Packers did a great job of limiting the second-year star's yardage. McMillan has now caught 30 passes over his last four games and is averaging exactly six per contest for the season. However, he scored both of his touchdowns in Week 4 against the Lions. He remains a high-end WR2 in most formats.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan's Recent Struggles Continue Against Packers
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan hauled in six of 11 targets for 58 yards in the 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. While McMillan secured enough short passes to salvage his stat line, he was unproductive downfield and in the red zone in Week 8. Since his monster game in Week 4, McMillan has caught 16 passes for 184 yards and no touchdowns, averaging under nine half-PPR fantasy points per game. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young has cooled off after a hot start, and the offensive line is currently battered by injuries, leaving Young with little time to push the ball downfield. While McMillan is still the Panthers' lead receiver, his status as a must-start wide receiver in fantasy has worn off after back-to-back games of lackluster production from this passing attack.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Paces pass catchers with modest yardage
metadata.description: McMillan brought in six of 11 targets for 57 yards in the Panthers' 27-19 loss to the Packers on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: McMillan led the Panthers in receiving yards despite generating a modest total, and the second-year wideout has now fallen under 60 receiving yards in consecutive games for the first time this season. He does have at least six grabs in three of the past four games and a trio of double-digit target tallies on the season, so he continues to sport a formidable fantasy floor despite Bryce Young's current struggles. Carolina's air attack may have a tough time bouncing back in Week 9, however, as the stingy Broncos defense comes to town on Sunday, Nov. 8.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Lined Up for Good Fantasy Outing in Week 8
metadata.description: Carolina wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan is set up to succeed in the team's Week 8 Thursday night clash against Green Bay. The Packers have struggled a bit to slow opposing fantasy wide receivers this season, even though they've allowed just 208 passing yards per contest. McMillan is coming off a down game against Tampa Bay in Week 7 - he mustered just 40 yards across four receptions and six targets. He's otherwise been a pretty solid fantasy starting option, and he could return to that level thanks to this week's matchup. McMillan could also take on more with wideout Jalen Coker dealing with a shoulder injury, although Coker doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday and was a full practice participant on Tuesday and Wednesday. McMillan sits as WR14 in our RotoBaller Week 8 rankings, so he's another Panther to be starting in all leagues this week.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan catches four passes in loss
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan caught four of six targets for 40 yards in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to Tampa Bay on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McMillan was largely held in check all day by the Tampa defense, as was the rest of the Carolina offense. It wasn't a great showing by the young receiver, but it didn't sink your week. He will look to improve on those numbers against the Packers on TNF.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Four catches in Week 7 loss
metadata.description: McMillan secured four of six targets for 40 yards in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: As the final score implies, it was a total washout for the Panthers in the divisional clash, making McMillan's modest numbers unsurprising. The 2025 first-round pick did tie for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in targets, but his receiving yardage total was his second lowest of the campaign. McMillan still sports an impressive 36-511-2 line on 54 targets heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the Packers on Thursday night.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Has Low Output in Blowout Loss to Bucs
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan posted four receptions (on six targets) for 40 yards (10.0 yards per catch) and did not find the end zone in a 43-13 blowout loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7. He played 38 offensive snaps. The lopsided loss made it difficult for any Panther player to put up large numbers on Sunday, but it was McMillan's second-lowest output of the 2026 season (two receptions for 17 yards in Week 3). Still, McMillan led Carolina in targets and tied for the team lead in receptions with running back Chuba Hubbard. Quarterback Bryce Young only threw for 163 yards on the day, and 50 of those came on his lone touchdown pass to tight end Darren Waller. This game is likely an anomaly, as the Panthers found themselves down 33-6 at halftime. McMillan will remain heavily involved in Carolina's passing game and is still a must-start player. He will look to bounce back on Thursday Night Football against the Green Bay Packers in Week 8.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Offers Upside in Week 7 Matchup
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan remains an effective fantasy asset as his team prepares for a Week 7 battle against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. McMillan had six receptions for 84 yards in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, which was a dip from his earlier production only because teammate Jalen Coker returned to the gridiron. Still, the 23-year-old should see his fair share of targets from Bryce Young against a struggling Buccaneers passing defense. He's a low-end WR2 with upside in Week 7.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Solid production with six catches
metadata.description: McMillan secured six of nine targets for 86 yards in the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McMillan tied for the team lead in receptions with Jalen Coker while finishing second to his talented position mate in receiving yards and targets. The 2025 first-round pick was coming off a career-best 14-catch, 192-yard performance that also included two touchdowns against the Lions back in Week 4, and he's gone for at least 75 receiving yards in four of his first five games of the campaign as a Week 7 home divisional showdown against the Buccaneers approaches.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan gains 86 yards in Week 6 win
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan caught six passes for 86 yards in a Week 6 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
metadata.analysis: McMillan has 75+ yards and 8+ targets in four of five games to start the season, a reliable floor in what has been a potent Carolina passing offense. He has not caught a touchdown yet with wide receiver Jalen Coker in the lineup, but McMillan's large frame and target rate indicate more could come in the future after scoring seven as a rookie.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Should See Reduced Volume Amid Teammate's Return
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan isn't likely to see the insane volume from last week again in Week 6. In Week 5, he caught 14 of his 16 targets for 192 yards and two touchdowns against the floundering Detroit Lions pass defense. He played that game without WR Jalen Coker, who actually out-targeted and outproduced him in Week 1. Coker suffered a quad injury in Week 3 after tying McMillan in targets and easily pacing him in catches, yards, and touchdowns in the first two weeks. McMillan hasn't been very consistent this season, evidenced by his mere 3.7 PPR fantasy points in Week 3. Still, he shouldn't be left out of starting lineups after his detonation in Week 4. His upside may not be that of a top-5 wideout when Coker is on the field, but he should sit in around WR2 range for the matchup with the Eagles in Week 6.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Poised to Continue Big Role with Panthers
metadata.description: The last time Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan was on the field, he shredded the Detroit Lions defense for 14 receptions for 192 yards (13.7 yards per reception) and two touchdowns on a Sunday Night Football win in Week 4. The Panthers had a bye week in Week 5, but get back to action against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. McMillan will look to continue his momentum, as he currently leads the Panthers in receptions (26) and receiving yards (385), and is tied for the team lead in touchdown catches (two). The Panthers are dealing with injuries to fellow wide receivers Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee). Leggete was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 3 due to a knee injury, while Coker missed the Week 4 contest against the Lions with an injury to his quadriceps. Ahead of Week 6, however, Coker got in a full practice session on Wednesday. Still, expect McMillan to be heavily involved for the Panthers against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan shreds Lions secondary Sunday night
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan collected 14 receptions on 16 targets for 192 yards and a pair of touchdowns in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
metadata.analysis: For those frustrated by McMillan's paltry output in Week 3, the second-year star erupted for career highs in receptions and yards Sunday night. He also recorded the second multi-touchdown game of his career. It's important to note that this performance came with both Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee) out, but McMillan still displayed his immense upside. He's a solid WR2 for fantasy purposes at present.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Career-best 192 yards, two TDs on SNF
metadata.description: McMillan caught 14 of 16 targets for 192 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
metadata.analysis: McMillan got open at will against Detroit's struggling secondary, setting career highs in catches, receiving yards and targets while posting his third multi-touchdown performance through 21 regular-season games. The 2025 first-round pick caught a 32-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter and a 10-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter. McMillan entered play Sunday with 23 targets through three games compared to 22 targets for fellow starting wide receiver Jalen Coker (quadriceps), who was inactive against the Lions. Coker will have an extra week to heal up during Carolina's Week 5 bye before possibly rejoining McMillan in Week 6 against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Has High Upside in Week 4
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan could get more work in Week 4 against the Detroit Lions, which could help him rebound from a quiet Week 3 performance. McMillan caught just 2-of-5 targets for a measly 17 yards in a 21-18 loss to the Cleveland Browns, but his target share should go up with fellow wideout Xavier Legette (knee) ruled out and Jalen Coker (quad) listed as questionable. Detroit's passing defense is allowing a league-high 299.3 yards per game, which opens the door for Bryce Young to find McMillan downfield early and often. The former first-round pick is a high-upside WR2 in Week 4.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Well-Positioned to Shake Off a Quiet Week 3
metadata.description: Three games into his second season, Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan has yet to find the end zone, and he is coming off a 17-yard performance in Sunday's loss to the Browns, the second-lowest total of his career. Somewhat surprisingly, it has been third-year undrafted receiver Jalen Coker (quad) who leads the team in targets, receptions, and yards to begin the year, but after suffering a minor quad strain on Sunday, his availability is in question for Week 4, potentially putting McMillan back in the primary pass-catching role from which he earned Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2025. However, a notable change since last season has been the growth of quarterback Bryce Young, who leads the league with 939 passing yards and is tied for fifth with seven passing touchdowns. If Coker is unable to play on Sunday night, McMillan could be in line for a week-winning performance against a Lions defense dealing with significant injuries in their secondary, making him RotoBaller's WR13 for the week.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan disappears in loss Sunday
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan caught 2-of-5 targets for just 17 yards in Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Cleveland Browns.
metadata.analysis: McMillan got shut down on Sunday. He was only able to catch two passes for just 17 yards against the Browns, despite being the team's clear WR1 after Jalen Coker (quad) left the game. He should bounce back in the near future, but it's possible that his week-to-week floor will be lower than managers hoped coming into the season.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Two catches in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: McMillan brought in two of five targets for 17 yards in the Panthers' 21-18 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: The Panthers' No. 1 receiver fell victim to a Browns defense that played aggressively for the second straight game. Cleveland brought pressure on Bryce Young throughout while recording a trio of sacks and picking him off once, and McMillan's production suffered as a result. McMillan's catch and receiving yardage totals tied for and qualified as the second-lowest figures of his career, respectively, making it an all-around forgettable afternoon for the second-year wideout. McMillan and the rest of the Panthers offense will look to regroup and atone for the stumble in a Week 4 primetime home showdown against the Lions next Sunday night, and McMillan will be in line for an even heavier workload than usual if Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is unable to suit up.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan a WR2 in Week 3
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan should be a solid WR2 in Week 3 against the Cleveland Browns. McMillan has gotten off to a bit of a slow start this season as he enters this week as the WR22. However, McMillan is fresh off a 10-target, 101-yard game in Week 2. The main thing missing for McMillan is touchdowns. At the rate quarterback Bryce Young is throwing touchdowns, it is only a matter of time before McMillan finds the end zone. The Browns have a solid secondary, but there is no one you should be afraid of for fantasy. This team is also allowing 34.65 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers through two weeks. McMillan is tied with fellow wideout Jalen Coker (ankle) for the team lead in targets through two games at 18. The volume will be there in Week 3. If he can find the end zone, McMillan could sneak into high-end WR2 territory.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Could See Larger Role in Week 3
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan saw a team-high 10 targets during last week's win over the Atlanta Falcons. McMillan hauled in five of those for 101 yards in the blowout victory. That was a strong game from McMillan, and it might get better for him in Week 3 against the Cleveland Browns. Fellow wideout Jalen Coker (ankle) is currently listed as questionable for Sunday's game. He was limited in practice on Wednesday with an ankle injury. If Coker gets downgraded, McMillan would be the focal point in the receiving game this weekend. If both are active, McMillan remains a strong WR2 against a shaky Browns defense.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan leads Panthers receivers in win
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5 of 10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McMillan's ten targets led the team, with Jalen Coker falling close behind with nine. It's a bummer he didn't connect on more than five, as he could have had a much bigger day. He and Coker are forming a formidable receiving duo in Carolina, and both are startable every week.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Clears century mark in win
metadata.description: McMillan brought in five of 10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McMillan's yardage total comfortably paced the Panthers on the afternoon, and the second-year pro also led the team in targets while checking in as the runner-up in receptions. He's posted five catches apiece in each of his first two games of the season and parlayed them into a solid 176 receiving yards on 18 targets, all numbers that only serve to further cement his status as an integral component of Carolina's air attack. McMillan will next take aim at the Browns' inconsistent defense in a Week 3 road matchup next Sunday.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Looking to Stay Productive Against The Falcons
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan caught five of eight targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears. While McMillan was productive, he took a backseat to teammate Jalen Coker (ankle), who caught eight passes for 138 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's loss. Coming off a rookie season where McMillan racked up 1,014 receiving yards and seven touchdowns, the 23-year-old is Carolina's WR1 and will look to reprise that role even with Coker cleared to play in Week 2 against the Falcons. Atlanta limited the Steelers to just 221 passing yards in the regular-season opener, but will have a tall task trying to slow a red-hot Panthers offense that erupted for 37 points last Sunday. McMillan is ranked WR23 in the latest RotoBaller Week 2 rankings and is a strong WR2 heading into fantasy football in Week 2.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Looking To Have Bigger Role in Week 2
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan could see an increased role in Week 2 with Jalen Coker's injury status still questionable. Coker had a breakout Week 1 against the Bears, while McMillan caught five passes for 75 yards and no touchdowns as Coker was the star receiver. After the game on Monday, Coker was seen in a walking boot and is nursing an ankle injury. He is questionable to play against the Falcons and was limited in Wednesday's practice. Should Coker be limited or forced to miss Week 2's contest, McMillan would get a huge boost as the No. 1 target for quarterback Bryce Young. How the split plays out between the two talented receivers remains to be seen but in Week 1 it was in favor of Coker. Look for a bounce back of sorts from McMillan this week.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Plays a Major Role on Offense
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan made a very positive impression as a rookie last year, and he continues to offer solid WR2 value in fantasy football leagues in 2026. McMillan opened the season with eight targets, five catches, and 75 yards in the Panthers' Week 1 contest against the Chicago Bears. He came on a little slow but finished incredibly strong, ranking second on the team in catches and yards behind Jalen Coker. He also played an impressive 82% snap share, which indicates that he should continue to occupy a major role going forward, presumably as Bryce Young's No. 1 receiver. The emergence of Coker could have a very slight impact on McMillan's stock, but we're still confident in him as fantasy WR2 with high volume and touchdown upside. He should benefit immensely from a Week 2 matchup against a suspect Atlanta Falcons team.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan hauls in five receptions in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Tetairoa McMillan hauled in five of his eight targets for 75 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
metadata.analysis: McMillan made the most of his sizeable volume in the Carolina passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic pass-catching options in the Carolina offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan - Salvages day in second half in Week 1
metadata.description: McMillan caught five of eight targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 59-37 loss to the Bears.
metadata.analysis: In the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history, McMillan had just one catch for 14 yards in the first half, but he was able to pad his numbers after halftime as the Panthers' offense tried in vain to keep pace. Jalen Coker (8-138-2 on nine targets) was Bryce Young's favorite target on the afternoon, but he and McMillan were the only two Carolina wide receivers to catch a pass in the contest, a good sign for the future volume of both. McMillan will look to build on this performance in Week 2 on the road against the Falcons.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan in a Smash Spot Against the Bears in Week 1
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan is set up for a strong Week 1 against a banged-up Chicago Bears secondary in Week 1. The Bears will be without safety Coby Bryant and cornerback Kyle Gordon for the regular-season opener and allowed the third most fantasy points to wideouts last season. Coming off an impressive rookie campaign where McMillan caught 70 passes for 1,014 yards and seven touchdowns in 17 games, the 23-year-old took home the 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Award. According to ESPN's Mike Kaye, McMillan will be used more in the slot in 2026, and Carolina wants to use the second-year wideout's size and strength to get the ball to him more in the middle of the field. McMillan is ranked as RotoBaller's WR23 in PPR formats, and fantasy managers should roll with him in all leagues as a borderline WR2 against the Bears in Week 1.

metadata.title: Tetairoa McMillan Set for More Versatile Usage in 2026?
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan could see more usage out of the slot in 2026, speculates ESPN's Mike Kaye. McMillan was used almost exclusively as an outside receiver as a rookie in 2025 and had plenty of success, recording 70 catches for 1,014 yards and seven touchdowns on 122 targets across 17 games. However, Kaye writes that the Panthers have spoken about wanting to use McMillan's size and strength to get him more targets in the middle of the field in his second season. McMillan already projects to be the dominant target-earner in Carolina's offense, as he finished with nearly 60 more targets than any other Panthers pass-catcher in 2025. If he does indeed see more slot usage and an even larger target share in 2026, McMillan could emerge as a fantasy WR1.
